source.topic: keep the fridge, lights, phone chargers and medical devices running during a power outage using a power inverter and the car already in your driveway
source.angle: the HONEST, safe version of the 'your car is a generator' trend - real wattage math for what actually fits, and the two safety rules the overclaiming competitors skip (never backfeed the breaker panel, never run the engine indoors). Differentiator against the crowded field of DIY-generator videos, several of which overclaim (e.g. tiny wind turbines 'powering any home').
source.research_note: Validated via tools/validate_topic.py --topic 'how to make a generator to power your home' --niche home-hacks --recent 90d --long-only -> VERDICT: GO (9/12). Autocompletes at rank 3, 5 small-channel breakouts in 90d (best 33.4x, 100,270v on 3,000 subs), on-topic median 4,283 views/day. Full evidence: docs/research/home-hacks-power-outage-2.json. First-pass phrasing ('power your home during an outage without a generator') came back NO-DEMAND - narrowed to the autocomplete-matched phrasing per validate_topic.py's own guidance. Landscape context: tools/yt_research.py --niche home-hacks --window 30d showed the 'kill mosquitoes the Amish way' angle currently cloned across 5 small channels (CROWDED) - avoided that angle in favor of this less-saturated one. Outlier data: docs/research/home-hacks-viral.json (365d) - Eli Yoder Construction's generator video is the #2 all-time outlier in the niche at 31.81x / 28,568 views per day.
